summary: This component fetches and displays comments from Bluesky (a social media platform) on a blog post. It converts the raw Bluesky API response into a threaded comment display, handling text formatting with links, embedded images, and proper nesting based on reply depth. The component gracefully handles loading states and errors without disrupting the page.

explanations.12: Bluesky uses byte offsets instead of character positions to mark where links and special text begin and end—this matters for emoji and accented characters which take multiple bytes each.
explanations.19: TextEncoder converts JavaScript strings into byte sequences so we can slice text at the exact byte positions Bluesky gives us, and TextDecoder converts those bytes back to readable strings.
explanations.26: This loops through each 'facet' (a marked section of text like a link) and builds an array of rendered parts—mixing plain text with interactive elements like links.
explanations.33: We search through all the features (styling/link info) associated with this text section to find if it contains a link, since a single section might have multiple types of formatting.
explanations.68: Instead of checking the type string directly (which wouldn't work because Bluesky's catch-all type for unknown embeds is just a plain string), we check if the 'external' property exists to confirm it's a link embed.
explanations.104: We extend the BlueskyReplyNode type by adding a 'depth' field to track how nested each comment is, so we can indent them visually in the UI.
explanations.109: We extract the unique post ID from the full URI by splitting on slashes and taking the last piece—it's the record key that identifies this specific post.
explanations.123: We use the depth value to indent nested replies progressively—each level deeper gets an additional 1.5rem of left padding.
explanations.206: This recursive function flattens the tree-like reply structure (replies can have replies) into a single flat array while remembering each comment's nesting level.
explanations.209: We spread the reply object (keeping all its data) and add a new 'depth' property to track how many levels deep this reply is nested.
explanations.229: We return null (render nothing) if there's no post ID to fetch or if fetching failed—silently skipping the comments section rather than showing an error.
explanations.230: While comments are still loading, show a simple loading message instead of nothing, so the user knows the component is working.
